laws.rule: Jakarta's air pollution regulation (Perda 2/2005, Article 13) declares public places, health facilities, workplaces, places of learning, children's activity areas, places of worship and public transport no-smoking areas. The managers of public places and workplaces must provide a separate smoking area.
laws.penalty_signal: Article 41(2) sets up to six months in custody or a fine of up to IDR 50,000,000 (about A$3,912, at IDR 12,780 per A$1, the rate implied by the RBA 30 October 2026 figure used in this repo's Rinjani record).

sources.title: Perda DKI Jakarta Nomor 2 Tahun 2005 tentang Pengendalian Pencemaran Udara

local-law.note: The detailed list of no-smoking places is in a governor's regulation (Pergub 75/2005, amended by Pergub 88/2010) that was not read today.
